correctness.rationale: A lax witness gives partial functions x→y and u→v that extend to total Boolean functions. Conversely, inclusion in the union of their two equality sets gives a valid lax witness, with overlaps permitted. The complements consist of exactly one row for each (x,u), determined uniquely by the two functions, so all sixteen size-12 envelopes are distinct, incomparable, and exhaust the maximal satisfying teams. Failure is hitting all sixteen complement rectangles. I independently maintained the antichain of minimal hitting sets while adding each edge: retain current members hitting the new edge, extend each missing member by every element of the edge, then delete supersets. This step is exact because every new transversal contains a previous minimal one. It returned 132 members with histogram 4:12, 5:16, 6:96, 8:8. Inclusion-exclusion over rectangle avoidance independently yielded 33,159 violating teams, hence 32,377 satisfying. All 32 symmetry actions were used; the fixed-point sum was 288, and the independently chosen minimum orbit masks and sizes matched every frozen table row. The eight-set witness is one of these irredundant blockers and therefore precludes any smaller uniform bound.
residual_risks: The certificate exhausts this labelled Boolean universe and the stated symmetry only; it establishes no larger-universe cutoff.

evidence: In a minimally unsatisfiable 2-CNF each literal appears at most twice (Abbasizanjani–Kullmann, Lemma 9.1). Their §1.1 gives the nonsingular B_n family, a cycle of equivalences with a final negation. Barlag et al. define the same propositional semantics and give the crude 2^n bound on team size, with general coherence/complexity results.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Four variables give 8 literals and hence at most 16 literal occurrences; every clause here uses two literals, so at most 8 clauses can occur in a minimal failure. B₄ fits along the bipartite square, attaining 8. Thus the exact sharp cutoff is already a direct corollary of older results. Neither the generic cutoff nor the propositional setting gives the labeled finite census.

value.rationale: The full Boolean cube is the canonical smallest propositional universe of the disjoint two-atom formula singled out in the coherence literature. Its minimal failures give precisely the forbidden basis, not only an instance test or a witness at the maximal size. The exact size distribution and natural equivalence classes provide a benchmark for comparing disjoint-attribute splits and their finite-size thresholds; the labeled satisfying count also measures the extent of overlap of the maximal teams. This value does not depend on crediting the already implied eight-row bound as new.
residual_risks: No generalization to larger domains or to arbitrary dependence formulas is inferred.
